name: The Warehouse

evidence.note: Review summary: large bar, elevated stage with good sound, and a dance floor.
Official site: up to 300 guests with 150+ seats on three raised tiers; a quoted review mentions plenty of standing room.
Visitor review says a band played songs you could dance to.

dancing.notes: There is standing room in front of the raised stage that reviewers describe as a dance floor, and fans dance to the cover bands. Tables must be reserved and cost extra.

description: A live-music club, bar and event space in Amityville village with a raised stage, a 40-foot bar, tiered seating and a kitchen, hosting local cover bands, tribute acts and themed brunches.
reviewNotes:
Added from Ira's List research (2026-10-03). Ira's List venue page (/the-warehouse) links to thewarehouseli.com/calendar, so 'Warehouse' is The Warehouse in Amityville, not another business with that name. Gigs this weekend: Taylor Swift Eras Drag Brunch (Sat and Sun) and Serve The Servants / Love Hate Love (Sat night); not checked on the venue calendar. Reviews say reserved tables carry a fee and food/drink minimums.

Directory research 2026-10-04: Email whtable@gmail.com is the site's general/private-event address; band booking is 203grille@gmail.com (ATTN: Band Booking). The site does not publish opening hours and Google only shows Sunday 6:30 PM-1 AM, so hours left out (it runs by event calendar). Photo 1 is the site's darkened black-and-white background image of the crowd; it shows the room well but is dim. The second photo is a singer on what looks like the venue's stage (from the site's music section). A white version of the logo is used in the header; we took the dark footer logo. Current description still accurate.
